question.text: When the price of the underlying commodity rises, the impact on option premiums is:

answer.text: Call premium rises, Put premium falls
Both call and put premiums rise
Call premium falls, Put premium rises
Both call and put premiums fall

explanation.text: The Logic: A rising underlying price increases call value (the right to buy at the strike becomes more valuable) and decreases put value (the right to sell at the strike becomes less valuable). The Trap: The impact is opposite for calls and puts. They do not move in the same direction when the underlying price changes, so options that assume parallel movement of both premiums are wrong. Note: This is why delta is positive for calls and negative for puts in the workbook - delta captures exactly this directional sensitivity of option price to underlying price movement.
